notes.meaning: David turns to the Lord as his safe hiding place and asks never to be disgraced. He pleads for rescue based on God's own righteousness and faithfulness to His promises, rather than any claim of personal merit. Putting our trust in the Lord means relying on His character to carry us through.

David asks God to bend down close to hear his weak voice, like someone leaning near a sickbed. He pleads for quick help because his danger is urgent. He asks God to be a solid cliff fortress where no enemy can reach him.

David declares that God is already his true rock and fortress, and he uses that fact to ask for ongoing guidance. He asks to be led for the sake of God's name, knowing that God's own honor is tied to keeping His promises. Faith boldly asks God to be what He has already proven Himself to be.

David prays to be pulled out of the hidden trap his enemies have secretly laid for him. He has no strength of his own to break free from their schemes. Only the Lord has the power to shatter the trap and rescue him.

David entrusts his life and inner spirit entirely into God's safe keeping, whether he lives or dies. He calls the Lord his Redeemer and the God of truth who never breaks His word. Jesus made these words famous by speaking them on the cross as He breathed His last.

David rejects worthless idols and empty superstitions, which can never give the help they promise. He detests relying on anything other than the true God. Instead, he places all his confidence in the Lord alone.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: In the Latin Vulgate and Douay-Rheims, the verse says God hates those who cling to vanities, rather than David stating his own hatred of them.

notes.meaning: David chooses to rejoice in God's faithful love because the Lord noticed his deep pain. When human friends looked away, God recognized his distress and cared for him. Knowing that God sees our deepest sorrows brings real joy in hard times.

God refused to abandon David into the hands of his foes. Instead, the Lord led him out of tight, cramped trouble and placed his feet in a wide, safe place. This broad room means relief, freedom, and protection from harm.

David returns to his immediate trouble and cries out for God's mercy. Endless weeping has blurred and weakened his eyes. His long sorrow has completely exhausted both his inner soul and his physical body.

David's days are eaten up by grief, and his years pass in heavy groaning. He admits that his own sin and weakness have drained his strength and made his bones waste away. Despair and guilt take a severe toll on the whole body.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following the Greek Septuagint and Latin Vulgate, older Catholic translations read that his strength failed through poverty or affliction rather than iniquity.

notes.meaning: David has become an object of mockery to his enemies and a shameful burden to his neighbors. Even his closest friends are terrified of being associated with him. When people spot him walking in the street, they run away to protect themselves.

People treat David as if he were already dead and wiped from their memory. He compares himself to a shattered clay pot that cannot be repaired. In the eyes of the world, he is completely useless and thrown away.

David overhears the slander and whispered plots of many enemies, leaving him surrounded by terror. Those in power conspire together against him. Their goal is not merely to defeat him, but to take his life.

Despite the terror and desertion around him, David renews his trust in the Lord. He openly confesses that the Lord is his God and his true defender. True faith clings to God even when every human support falls away.

David acknowledges that all the changes, seasons, and days of his life are directed by God's sovereign care. Because his enemies do not hold his destiny, they cannot end his life before God's appointed time. He asks the Lord to step in and rescue him from his pursuers.

David asks God to smile on him and show him the warmth of His gracious presence. He prays for deliverance based solely on God's steadfast love and mercy. He knows salvation comes from God's goodness, never from human merit.

David asks that his trust in God will not end in public shame, since he has cried out to the Lord for help. Instead, he asks that the wicked be confounded and silenced by death. When evil men are silenced in the grave, their ability to harm the innocent comes to an end.
David prays for lying lips to be struck dumb. His accusers spoke arrogant, bitter words against him with pride and contempt. He asks God to vindicate the upright and put an end to deceitful attacks.

David is filled with wonder at the vast treasure of goodness God has stored up for those who revere Him. God does not keep this kindness hidden forever; He brings it out openly before everyone to help those who seek refuge in Him. God's blessings are more than enough for every need.

God hides His people in the safe shelter of His own presence, far away from human plots. He protects them like honored guests inside His royal pavilion, sheltered from slander and arguing tongues. Those who live close to God find peace that hostile words cannot touch.

David praises the Lord for showing him wonderful, faithful love. God guarded him so completely that he was as safe as someone protected within a strongly fortified city. God's protection is stronger than any stone walls or gates.

In a moment of hurried panic and fear, David thought that God had cast him out and stopped watching over him. Yet even though his faith wavered, God still listened when he cried out for mercy. God's grace is greater than our moments of sudden fear.

David urges all of God's holy people to love the Lord deeply. The Lord guards and keeps those who remain faithful to Him, but He brings full judgment on the arrogant. Experiencing God's deliverance makes believers eager to praise Him and encourage others.

David concludes by telling everyone who waits on the Lord to be brave and strong. God promises to pour strength into the hearts of those who keep their hope fixed on Him. Patient trust in the Lord gives us courage to face any trial.
